name: Rodge Andru P. Viloria
shortBio: Artist and designer working across digital illustration, graphic design, and poster composition — with an editorial eye for restraint, proportion, and quiet impact.
fullBiography: The practice began in formal visual communication study and matured through independent work. Early assignments taught structure; later years taught judgment — which images deserve public space, and which should stay private. Today the studio operates as a curated exhibition: fewer pieces, clearer intention, and presentation paced like rooms in a gallery. Each work is finished with the same questions: does the composition hold at a distance, does the type earn its place, and does the silence around the image feel intentional.
introduction: The work comes first. Context follows only when it deepens understanding — never when it turns the exhibition into a résumé. Visitors meet a practice shaped by editorial sensibility: careful pacing, measured hierarchy, and respect for the original image.
philosophy: Images should hold attention without noise. Composition leads; decoration follows only when it earns its place. Each piece is paced like a room in a gallery: clear entry, intentional pause, and space to leave.

skills.label: Digital Illustration
skills.description: Narrative images built for mood, character, and quiet detail — composed to hold attention without spectacle.

skills.label: Graphic Design
skills.description: Visual systems where type, space, and hierarchy do the work. Clarity over ornament.

skills.label: Poster Design
skills.description: Single-frame compositions meant to hold attention from a distance — horizon, mark, and type in measured balance.

skills.label: Anime
skills.description: Stylized figure work informed by pacing, gesture, and line — atmospheric rather than crowded.

timeline.title: Foundations
timeline.description: Began formal study in visual communication, grounding daily practice in drawing, composition, and typography.

timeline.title: Craft discipline
timeline.description: Shifted from assignment volume to deliberate iteration — fewer studies, stronger finishes, clearer visual judgment.

timeline.title: Independent practice
timeline.description: Moved from assignment-driven work to a curated body of illustration and poster studies under Reshz Studio.

timeline.title: Studio focus
timeline.description: Refined the exhibition approach — fewer pieces, clearer intention, and careful presentation across print and screen.

timeline.title: Public exhibition
timeline.description: Opened this site as a living archive of selected creative work — a digital gallery rather than a catalogue dump.

education.description: Emphasis on composition, typography, and image-making for print and screen. Formal study that became the foundation for independent studio practice.

experience.summary: Produces digital illustration, graphic design, and poster work with an editorial, exhibition-first approach. Responsible for concept, composition, finish, and presentation across selected pieces.
Developed foundational skills in drawing, typography, and layout through formal coursework and self-directed poster and illustration studies that later informed the studio archive.

values.title: Restraint
values.description: Clarity over volume. Every element must justify its presence.

values.title: Craft
values.description: Proportion, pacing, and finish matter as much as the idea.

values.title: Intention
values.description: Work should feel considered — never decorative for its own sake.

values.title: Respect
values.description: For the image, the viewer, and the time both share.

funFacts.label: Drawing
funFacts.detail: Sketchbooks remain the quietest part of the practice — where ideas arrive without pressure to publish.

funFacts.label: Music
funFacts.detail: Long work sessions usually begin with the same short playlist. Rhythm sets the pace of the composition pass.

funFacts.label: Coffee
funFacts.detail: Preferred ritual before any serious composition pass.

funFacts.label: Books
funFacts.detail: Editorial layouts and museum catalogues are frequent references for spacing, hierarchy, and silence.

currentFocus: Curating a focused exhibition of illustration and poster work — and refining how each piece is seen.
